source.title: Do LLMs Know Their Vulnerable Scenarios?
source.authors: Ziheng Peng; Huiqi Deng; Haoran Jing; Xuan-Kun Rong; Jia-Hui Han; Xi-Ting Wang; Na Zou; Xia Hu

record.file_problem: none; the paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It causally intervenes on scenario-derived directions and SAE concept directions and measures refusal scores, using a different direction-finding method and target than the original claim. It does not intervene on the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The tested directions are scenario-wrapped-minus-direct-harmful directions or SAE concept decoder directions, not the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. The study reports refusal-score changes from these interventions, but does not ablate the claimed direction, induce refusals on harmless requests, or test general capability. Scenario-conditioned attack success rates are omitted because they do not measure whether attacks suppress the claimed direction.
record.test_reason: The study scores refusal with a supervised logistic-probe CAV fit at the final layer on refusal vs. non-refusal examples, and reports its own method's attack success rates. That probe is not the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. The study never ablates that direction, adds it to harmless prompts, edits weights, or checks capabilities. Its steering experiments add scenario or SAE directions and read the CAV score, not response-level refusal. This is closest to V3 (jailbreak framings lower an internal refusal score), but it uses a different refusal direction and a score rather than behaviour, so it does not test the claimed direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that scenario-direction steering consistently reduces refusal scores, that SAE concept attribution can find refusal-suppressing concepts, and that the scenarios translated from them raise black-box ASR by up to 18.2 points and transfer to closed models. They frame their refusal measure as a refusal direction in the sense of prior work, but it is a supervised CAV, not the difference-in-means direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses scenario-wrapped versus direct harmful-prompt differences and SAE concept decoder directions, rather than harmful-minus-harmless mean activations; adds directions to prompt-token representations and measures a refusal CAV score rather than removing a direction and measuring refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Scenario direction effects vary substantially across the 12 scenarios; the reported strongest SAE-concept suppression also differs by model, reaching up to ∼ 30% for LLaMA-3.1-8B and Ministral-3-8B but only ∼ 2% for Qwen3.5-9B.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 1, an actual LaTeX-wrapped prompt lowers the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct CAV refusal score from +11.46 to +1.18. Steering along the LaTeX scenario direction lowers it to +5.43.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scenario-wrapped jailbreak prompts lower a final-layer probe-based refusal score, and steering along the scenario direction partly reproduces this.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding scenario-derived directions at layer 27 lowers the CAV refusal score by between −11.9 and −0.04, depending on the scenario.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some scenario-derived residual directions causally lower a probe-based refusal score, with scenario-dependent magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: The strongest single SAE concept lowers the refusal score by about 30% in LLaMA and Ministral, but only about 2% in Qwen. Most concepts change it by under 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-score suppression by single SAE concepts sits in a thin tail of concepts and its depth is model-dependent.

record.problems: The steering experiments report refusal-CAV scores rather than response-level refusal or compliance, and the scenario-direction test is on one model with 50 selected high-refusal requests. The strongest SAE effects are reported as approximate maxima; uncertainty estimates for these intervention results are not stated. The study does not test general capability retention.
record.rows_left_out: Scenario-conditioned jailbreak ASRs in Tables 1, 2, and 7 and the AgentHarm results in Tables 9–10 are omitted: they measure attack or agent outcomes, not whether the claimed refusal direction is suppressed. Figure 3 and Figure 7 combination results are likewise attack-success outcomes, not measurements of the claimed direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, no ablation, no induction of refusal on harmless prompts, no capability check.
The study shows scenario wrapping lowers a CAV refusal score, but not along the difference-in-means direction. No robustness training against ablation.
Refusal geometry is not tested. The SAE concept tail measures concepts that modulate refusal, not multiple refusal directions.
Harmfulness and refusal are not measured separately.
Probe accuracy is compared between base and instruct models, but transfer of a refusal direction is not tested.

missing.what: Refusal score for an actual LaTeX-wrapped prompt versus the direct prompt (11.46 → 1.18) and versus steering (5.43). This would be needed if the probe direction were ever accepted as a stand-in for V3.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The study relies on a linear refusal representation (the CAV) as a measuring tool, and its headline results are its own method's ASR. The reader set every version to not_tested while still calling the relation 'tests', which is inconsistent. Measure caveat: the CAV score is not a behavioural refusal rate, and the authors say the steering experiment tests representation-level control rather than jailbreak rate.

versions.untested_parts: Does not find or ablate the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, test its addition, or measure compliance after its removal.
No weight-edit ablation or released-model abliteration evaluation.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not test the geometry or number of refusal directions as affine, conic, or dominant-plus-other structures. Its multiple scenario concepts are not shown to be multiple refusal directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Scenario transfer is tested, but transfer of the claimed refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is not.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing to test whether a removable direction forms.
Does not test the claim in reasoning models.
